symptoms.symptom: Surface units will not maintain a rolling boil or cooking is slow

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Use pans which are absolutely flat and match the diameter of the surface unit selected.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Improper cookware being used."

symptoms.symptom: Surface units do not work properly

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Cooktop controls improperly set.
remedies: Check to see the correct control is set for the surface unit you are using.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Cooktop controls improperly set."

symptoms.symptom: Tiny scratches or metal marks (may appear as cracks) or abrasions on radiant cooktop glass surface

causes.label: Incorrect cleaning methods being used.
remedies: Use recommended cleaning procedures.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Incorrect cleaning methods being used."

causes.label: Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop.
remedies: Be sure cookware bottoms and cookware are clean before use.
Use cookware with smooth bottoms.
Tiny scratches are not removable but will become less visible in time as a result of cleaning.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Cookware with rough bottoms being used or coarse particles (salt or sand) were between the cookware and the surface of the cooktop."

causes.label: Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Cookware has been slid across the cooktop surface."

symptoms.symptom: Areas of discoloration or dark streaks on the cooktop

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Marks from aluminum and copper pans as well as mineral deposits from water or food can be removed with the cleaning cream.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Improper cookware being used."

causes.label: Hot surface on a model with a light-colored cooktop.
remedies: This is normal.
The surface may appear discolored when it is hot.
This is temporary and will disappear as the glass cools.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Hot surface on a model with a light-colored cooktop."

causes.label: Food spillovers not cleaned before next use.
remedies: See the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Food spillovers not cleaned before next use."

causes.label: Incorrect cleaning methods being used.
remedies: Use recommended cleaning procedures.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Incorrect cleaning methods being used."

causes.label: Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop.
remedies: See the Glass surface – potential for permanent damage section in the Cleaning the glass cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Hot cooktop came into contact with plastic placed on the hot cooktop."

causes.label: Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop.
remedies: Call a qualified technician for replacement.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Hot sugar mixture spilled on the cooktop."

symptoms.symptom: Frequent cycling off and on of surface units

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: Use only flat cookware to minimize cycling.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Improper cookware being used."

causes.label: Improper cookware being used.
remedies: The glass cooktop surface may seem hotter than you are used to.
This is normal.
Use pans which are absolutely flat.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Improper cookware being used."

causes.label: Cooktop controls improperly set.
remedies: When the knob is in the OFF position, it must be pushed in before it can be turned.
When the knob is in any other position, it can be turned without being pushed in.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 12: "Cooktop controls improperly set."
